items.text: The process that stamps rows with the source label 'HQ' matches every real (non-placeholder) row in the table exactly, and its start date matches two default rows precisely. This is very likely the real, currently active process updating the table, even though its own original data sources cannot be located anywhere in the Oracle database.

Two processes could plausibly update this table, but the evidence clearly favors one. The other process reads from a staging table that has been empty and unused since 2015. That process is confirmed dead, not just unlikely.

A generic process that creates placeholder rows matches one unapproved row created in 2019, but that same row was later updated by the 'HQ' process. So something else touched the row after it was created; the placeholder process alone does not fully explain it.

The orchestration code explicitly notes that this table's older, dead process was intentionally decommissioned on the same date its staging table went silent, not simply abandoned. This was part of a coordinated retirement across several related tables around the same time (including POS_ITEM_TYPE, TX_TYPE, GL Dept, GL Acct, Link Code and Terminal), which show the same pattern of an unresolved original data source.
One deliberate 'unknown value' placeholder row exists, the same convention used across every similar table analyzed so far

A related process for a connected table was found to pull its data from a specific external system named HQAnalytics, and stamps the same source label ('HQ') seen on this table. Neither of this table's own updating processes shows that same explicit connection, so a link to the same external system is plausible but not confirmed.
